sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mokṣaḥ pitāmahenokta upāyān nānupāyataḥ tam upāyaṃ yathānyāyaṃ śrotum icchāmi bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Liberation, O grandsire, has been declared by you as attainable through right means, not without means. That means, just as it truly is, I wish to hear, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tvayy evaitan mahāprājña yuktaṃ nipuṇadarśanam yad upāyena sarvārthān nityaṃ mṛgayase 'nagha
english: Bhīṣma said: In you alone, O greatly wise one, this keen insight is fitting, that by right means you ever seek out all your ends, O sinless one.

sanskrit: karaṇe ghaṭasya yā buddhir ghaṭotpattau na sānagha evaṃ dharmābhyupāyeṣu nānyad dharmeṣu kāraṇam
english: The knowledge that goes into the making of a pot is not the same as what brings the pot into being, O sinless one. So too with the means to righteousness: for the duties themselves there is no other cause than these.

sanskrit: pūrve samudre yaḥ panthā na sa gacchati paścimam ekaḥ panthā hi mokṣasya tan me vistarataḥ śṛṇu
english: The road that leads to the eastern sea does not lead to the western. But the path of liberation is one alone; hear it from me in full.

sanskrit: kṣamayā krodham ucchindyāt kāmaṃ saṃkalpavarjanāt sattvasaṃsevanād dhīro nidrām ucchetum arhati
english: By forbearance let one root out anger; desire, by renouncing the will that craves; and the steadfast man, by cultivating goodness, is fit to root out sloth.

sanskrit: apramādād bhayaṃ rakṣec chvāsaṃ kṣetrajñaśīlanāt icchāṃ dveṣaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca dhairyeṇa vinivartayet
english: By vigilance let him ward off fear, and the breath by the discipline of the knower of the field; longing, aversion, and desire let him turn back by firmness.

sanskrit: bhramaṃ pramoham āvartam abhyāsād vinivartayet nidrāṃ ca pratibhāṃ caiva jñānābhyāsena tattvavit
english: Confusion, delusion, and the whirling of the mind let him turn back by practice; and sleep too, and idle fancy, the knower of truth turns back by the practice of knowledge.

sanskrit: upadravāṃs tathā rogān hitajīrṇamitāśanāt lobhaṃ mohaṃ ca saṃtoṣād viṣayāṃs tattvadarśanāt
english: Afflictions and diseases he conquers by eating what is wholesome, well-digested, and measured; greed and delusion by contentment; the objects of sense by the vision of truth.

sanskrit: anukrośād adharmaṃ ca jayed dharmam upekṣayā āyatyā ca jayed āśām arthaṃ saṅgavivarjanāt
english: By compassion let him conquer unrighteousness, and righteousness by detachment; hope he conquers by looking to the future, and gain by renouncing attachment.

sanskrit: anityatvena ca snehaṃ kṣudhaṃ yogena paṇḍitaḥ kāruṇyenātmano mānaṃ tṛṣṇāṃ ca paritoṣataḥ
english: By reflecting on impermanence the wise man conquers fondness, and hunger by yoga; by compassion he conquers his own pride, and thirst by full contentment.

sanskrit: utthānena jayet tandrīṃ vitarkaṃ niścayāj jayet maunena bahubhāṣyaṃ ca śauryeṇa ca bhayaṃ jayet
english: By exertion let him conquer drowsiness, and doubt by resolve; idle talk he conquers by silence, and fear by valor.

sanskrit: yacched vāṅmanasī buddhyā tāṃ yacchej jñānacakṣuṣā jñānam ātmā mahān yacchet taṃ yacchec chāntir ātmanaḥ
english: Let him restrain speech and mind by the intellect, and restrain the intellect by the eye of knowledge; the great Self restrains knowledge, and that Self the peace of the soul restrains.

sanskrit: tad etad upaśāntena boddhavyaṃ śucikarmaṇā yogadoṣān samucchidya pañca yān kavayo viduḥ
english: This is to be understood by one who has grown calm, whose actions are pure, having rooted out the five flaws of yoga that the seers have known.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca bhayaṃ svapnaṃ ca pañcamam parityajya niṣeveta tathemān yogasādhanān
english: Desire, anger, greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth—having abandoned these, let him cultivate the following aids to yoga:

sanskrit: dhyānam adhyayanaṃ dānaṃ satyaṃ hrīr ārjavaṃ kṣamā śaucam āhārataḥ śuddhir indriyāṇāṃ ca saṃyamaḥ
english: Meditation, study, giving, truth, modesty, uprightness, forbearance, purity, cleanness in food, and restraint of the senses.

sanskrit: etair vivardhate tejaḥ pāpmānam apahanti ca sidhyanti cāsya saṃkalpā vijñānaṃ ca pravartate
english: By these his inner radiance grows and his sin is dispelled; his purposes are accomplished, and true discernment arises in him.

sanskrit: dhūtapāpaḥ sa tejasvī laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ kāmakrodhau vaśe kṛtvā ninīṣed brahmaṇaḥ padam
english: With his sins shaken off, radiant, eating sparingly, his senses mastered, having brought desire and anger under his sway, let him seek to reach the abode of Brahman.

sanskrit: amūḍhatvam asaṅgitvaṃ kāmakrodhavivarjanam adainyam anudīrṇatvam anudvego vyavasthitiḥ
english: Freedom from delusion, freedom from attachment, the renouncing of desire and anger, absence of meanness, absence of arrogance, freedom from agitation, and steadiness—

sanskrit: eṣa mārgo hi mokṣasya prasanno vimalaḥ śuciḥ tathā vākkāyamanasāṃ niyamaḥ kāmato 'nyathā
english: this is the path of liberation, serene, spotless, and pure; and so too the restraint of speech, body, and mind. To act from desire is the contrary way.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādaṃ devalasyāsitasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very matter they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue between Nārada and Asita Devala.

sanskrit: āsīnaṃ devalaṃ vṛddhaṃ buddhvā buddhimatāṃ varaḥ nāradaḥ paripapraccha bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayam
english: Seeing the aged Devala seated, Nārada, the best of the wise, questioned him about the origin and dissolution of beings.

sanskrit: kutaḥ sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ brahman sthāvarajaṅgamam pralaye ca kam abhyeti tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: From what was this universe of moving and unmoving things created, O brahman? And into what does it pass at the dissolution? Of this may your honor instruct me.

sanskrit: asita uvāca yebhyaḥ sṛjati bhūtāni kālo bhāvapracoditaḥ mahābhūtāni pañceti tāny āhur bhūtacintakāḥ
english: Asita said: Those from which Time, impelled by the inner nature of things, brings forth beings—the five great elements—these the contemplators of being declare them to be.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ sṛjati bhūtāni kāla ātmapracoditaḥ etebhyo yaḥ paraṃ brūyād asad brūyād asaṃśayam
english: From these Time, impelled by itself, brings forth beings; and whoever should speak of anything beyond these would, beyond doubt, be speaking of what is not.

sanskrit: viddhi nārada pañcaitāñ śāśvatān acalān dhruvān mahatas tejaso rāśīn kālaṣaṣṭhān svabhāvataḥ
english: Know, Nārada, these five to be eternal, unmoving, fixed, vast masses of energy, with Time as the sixth, such by their own nature.

sanskrit: āpaś caivāntarikṣaṃ ca pṛthivī vāyupāvakau asiddhiḥ param etebhyo bhūtebhyo muktasaṃśayam
english: Water, the atmosphere, earth, wind, and fire—beyond these elements there is no establishment of anything else; of this be free from doubt.

sanskrit: nopapattyā na vā yuktyā tv asad brūyād asaṃśayam vettha tān abhinirvṛttān ṣaḍ ete yasya rāśayaḥ
english: Neither by argument nor by reasoning could one, beyond doubt, affirm what is not. Know these to be wholly manifested—he of whom these six are the masses.

sanskrit: pañcaiva tāni kālaś ca bhāvābhāvau ca kevalau aṣṭau bhūtāni bhūtānāṃ śāśvatāni bhavāpyayau
english: Those five, and Time, and pure being and non-being—these are the eight that constitute the eternal coming-to-be and passing-away of beings.

sanskrit: abhāvād bhāviteṣv eva tebhyaś ca prabhavanty api vinaṣṭo 'pi ca tāny eva jantur bhavati pañcadhā
english: From non-being into the things brought into being, and from these they arise again; and even when destroyed, the creature becomes again just these same, fivefold.

sanskrit: tasya bhūmimayo dehaḥ śrotram ākāśasaṃbhavam sūryaś cakṣur asur vāyur adbhyas tu khalu śoṇitam
english: Its body is made of earth; its hearing arises from space; the sun is its eye, the wind its vital breath, and its blood, indeed, comes from the waters.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī nāsikākarṇau tvag jihveti ca pañcamī indriyāṇīndriyārthānāṃ jñānāni kavayo viduḥ
english: The two eyes, the nose, the ears, the skin, and the tongue as the fifth—these the seers know to be the senses, the faculties of knowing the objects of sense.

sanskrit: darśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ sparśanaṃ rasanaṃ tathā upapattyā guṇān viddhi pañca pañcasu pañcadhā
english: Seeing, hearing, smelling, touching, and likewise tasting—by reasoning know the five qualities in the five, fivefold.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ gandho rasaḥ sparśaḥ śabdaś caivātha tadguṇāḥ indriyair upalabhyante pañcadhā pañca pañcabhiḥ
english: Form, smell, taste, touch, and sound—these are their qualities; they are apprehended by the senses, the five by the five in fivefold ways.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ gandhaṃ rasaṃ sparśaṃ śabdaṃ caitāṃs tu tadguṇān indriyāṇi na budhyante kṣetrajñas tais tu budhyate
english: Form, smell, taste, touch, and sound—these qualities the senses themselves do not perceive; it is the knower of the field who perceives them through the senses.

sanskrit: cittam indriyasaṃghātāt paraṃ tasmāt paraṃ manaḥ manasas tu parā buddhiḥ kṣetrajño buddhitaḥ paraḥ
english: Beyond the aggregate of the senses is thought; beyond that is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and the knower of the field is higher than the intellect.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ cetayate jantur indriyair viṣayān pṛthak vicārya manasā paścād atha buddhyā vyavasyati indriyair upalabdhārthān sarvān yas tv adhyavasyati
english: First the creature becomes aware, through the senses, of objects severally; then, having pondered them with the mind, it determines them with the intellect—it is the intellect that resolves upon all the objects grasped by the senses.

sanskrit: cittam indriyasaṃghātaṃ mano buddhiṃ tathāṣṭamīm aṣṭau jñānendriyāṇy āhur etāny adhyātmacintakāḥ
english: Thought, the aggregate of the senses, the mind, and the intellect as the eighth—these eight they call the organs of knowledge, the contemplators of the inner self.

sanskrit: pāṇipādaṃ ca pāyuś ca mehanaṃ pañcamaṃ mukham iti saṃśabdyamānāni śṛṇu karmendriyāṇy api
english: The hands and feet, the anus, the organ of generation, and the mouth as the fifth—hear now these, named in order, the organs of action.

sanskrit: jalpanābhyavahārārthaṃ mukham indriyam ucyate gamanendriyaṃ tathā pādau karmaṇaḥ karaṇe karau
english: For the sake of speaking and of eating, the mouth is called an organ; the feet are the organ of motion, and the hands are the instruments of action.

sanskrit: pāyūpasthau visargārtham indriye tulyakarmaṇī visarge ca purīṣasya visarge cābhikāmike
english: The anus and the genital are two organs of like function, both serving discharge—the one in the voiding of excrement, the other in the discharge of desire.

sanskrit: balaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ ṣaḍ etāni vācā samyag yathāgamam jñānaceṣṭendriyaguṇāḥ sarve saṃśabditā mayā
english: Strength is the sixth—these six have I named in speech rightly, according to tradition; all the faculties of knowledge, of action, and their qualities have I declared.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ svakarmabhyaḥ śramād uparamo yadā bhavatīndriyasaṃnyāsād atha svapiti vai naraḥ
english: When, through weariness, the senses cease from their own functions, then by the withdrawal of the senses a man falls asleep.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ vyuparame mano 'nuparataṃ yadi sevate viṣayān eva tad vidyāt svapnadarśanam
english: When, the senses having ceased, the mind has not ceased but still dwells upon the objects of sense—that one should know to be the seeing of dreams.

sanskrit: sāttvikāś caiva ye bhāvās tathā rājasatāmasāḥ karmayuktān praśaṃsanti sāttvikān itarāṃs tathā
english: As for the states that are of goodness, of passion, and of darkness—men praise the sattvic ones as bound up with right action, and the others likewise according to their kind.

sanskrit: ānandaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiḥ pratipattiḥ parā gatiḥ sāttvikasya nimittāni bhāvān saṃśrayate smṛtiḥ
english: Joy, the accomplishment of deeds, attainment, and the highest goal—these are the marks of the sattvic man; memory takes refuge in his states of being.

sanskrit: jantuṣv ekatameṣv evaṃ bhāvā ye vidhim āsthitāḥ bhāvayor īpsitaṃ nityaṃ pratyakṣagamanaṃ dvayoḥ
english: In each several creature the states that abide by their ordinance—of the two states, the constant desired aim is the direct attaining of both.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi ca bhāvāś ca guṇāḥ saptadaśa smṛtāḥ teṣām aṣṭādaśo dehī yaḥ śarīre sa śāśvataḥ
english: The senses and the states of being are reckoned as seventeen qualities; the eighteenth of them is the embodied one, who within the body is eternal.

sanskrit: atha vā saśarīrās te guṇāḥ sarve śarīriṇām saṃśritās tadviyoge hi saśarīrā na santi te
english: Or else all those qualities are bodied together with the embodied beings, dwelling in them; for at their separation from the body those bodied qualities are no more.

sanskrit: atha vā saṃnipāto 'yaṃ śarīraṃ pāñcabhautikam ekaś ca daśa cāṣṭau ca guṇāḥ saha śarīriṇām ūṣmaṇā saha viṃśo vā saṃghātaḥ pāñcabhautikaḥ
english: Or else this body is a conjunction made of the five elements; and the qualities, nineteen together with the embodied ones, or with the bodily heat as the twentieth, form the aggregate made of the five elements.

sanskrit: mahān saṃdhārayaty etac charīraṃ vāyunā saha tasyāsya bhāvayuktasya nimittaṃ dehabhedane
english: The Great One, together with the breath, sustains this body; and of this being, joined with its states, there is a cause for the body's breaking apart.

sanskrit: yathaivotpadyate kiṃ cit pañcatvaṃ gacchate tathā puṇyapāpavināśānte puṇyapāpasamīritam dehaṃ viśati kālena tato 'yaṃ karmasaṃbhavam
english: Even as a thing comes into being, so too it dissolves into the five elements; at the ending of the exhaustion of merit and demerit, impelled by merit and demerit, in due time it enters a body—and thence is it born of its own deeds.

sanskrit: hitvā hitvā hy ayaṃ praiti dehād dehaṃ kṛtāśrayaḥ kālasaṃcoditaḥ kṣetrī viśīrṇād vā gṛhād gṛham
english: Forsaking body after body, this one passes on, taking a new support; the lord of the field, urged on by Time, moves from one dwelling to another, as from a worn-out house to a new home.

sanskrit: tatra naivānutapyante prājñā niścitaniścayāḥ kṛpaṇās tv anutapyante janāḥ saṃbandhimāninaḥ
english: At this the wise, whose conclusions are firmly settled, do not grieve; but the wretched grieve—folk who fancy themselves bound by kinship.

sanskrit: na hy ayaṃ kasya cit kaś cin nāsya kaś cana vidyate bhavaty eko hy ayaṃ nityaṃ śarīre sukhaduḥkhabhāk
english: For this one belongs to no one, and to it no one belongs; it remains ever alone within the body, the partaker of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: naiva saṃjāyate jantur na ca jātu vipadyate yāti deham ayaṃ bhuktvā kadā cit paramāṃ gatim
english: The creature is never truly born, nor does it ever perish; this one passes from body to body, and, having had its enjoyment, attains at last the highest goal.

sanskrit: puṇyapāpamayaṃ dehaṃ kṣapayan karmasaṃcayāt kṣīṇadehaḥ punar dehī brahmatvam upagacchati
english: Wearing away the body made of merit and demerit through the spending of its store of deeds, the embodied one, his body exhausted, attains again to the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: puṇyapāpakṣayārthaṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ jñānaṃ vidhīyate tatkṣaye hy asya paśyanti brahmabhāve parāṃ gatim
english: For the spending away of merit and demerit the knowledge of Sāṃkhya is enjoined; for at its exhaustion they behold his supreme goal in the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhrātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā jñātayaḥ suhṛdas tathā arthahetor hatāḥ krūrair asmābhiḥ pāpabuddhibhiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Brothers, fathers, sons, kinsmen, and friends—for the sake of wealth they were slain by us, cruel men of sinful mind.

sanskrit: yeyam arthodbhavā tṛṣṇā katham etāṃ pitāmaha nivartayema pāpaṃ hi tṛṣṇayā kāritā vayam
english: This thirst that springs from wealth—how, O grandsire, are we to turn it back? For it was by thirst that we were made to do the sin.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gītaṃ videharājena māṇḍavyāyānupṛcchate
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, sung by the king of Videha to Māṇḍavya, who had questioned him.

sanskrit: susukhaṃ bata jīvāmi yasya me nāsti kiṃ cana mithilāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ na me dahyati kiṃ cana
english: Most happily, indeed, do I live, I who possess nothing at all; though Mithilā be ablaze, nothing of mine is burned.

sanskrit: arthāḥ khalu samṛddhā hi bāḍhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vijānatām asamṛddhās tv api sadā mohayanty avicakṣaṇān
english: Riches, indeed, when abundant, are surely a sore grief to those who understand; yet even when not abundant they ever delude those without discernment.

sanskrit: yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām
english: Whatever pleasure of desire there is in the world, and whatever great pleasure there is of heaven—these are not worth a sixteenth part of the bliss that comes from the destruction of thirst.

sanskrit: yathaiva śṛṅgaṃ goḥ kāle vardhamānasya vardhate tathaiva tṛṣṇā vittena vardhamānena vardhate
english: Even as the horn of an ox grows as the beast grows in time, so does thirst grow along with growing wealth.

sanskrit: kiṃ cid eva mamatvena yadā bhavati kalpitam tad eva paritāpāya nāśe saṃpadyate punaḥ
english: Whatever has once been claimed as 'mine' through the sense of possession—that very thing, when it is lost, becomes again a cause of torment.

sanskrit: na kāmān anurudhyeta duḥkhaṃ kāmeṣu vai ratiḥ prāpyārtham upayuñjīta dharme kāmaṃ vivarjayet
english: Let one not give way to desires; for delight in desires is suffering. Having gained wealth, let him employ it in righteousness, and abandon desire.

sanskrit: vidvān sarveṣu bhūteṣu vyāghramāṃsopamo bhavet kṛtakṛtyo viśuddhātmā sarvaṃ tyajati vai saha
english: The wise man should be toward all creatures as one is toward tiger's flesh; having done what is to be done, his self made pure, he forsakes all things together.

sanskrit: ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā śokānandau priyāpriye bhayābhaye ca saṃtyajya saṃpraśānto nirāmayaḥ
english: Forsaking both truth and falsehood, sorrow and joy, the pleasant and the unpleasant, and casting away both fear and security, he becomes wholly tranquil and free of affliction.

sanskrit: yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ yo 'sau prāṇāntiko rogas tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham
english: That which is hard for the foolish to forsake, which does not decay even as the man decays, that disease which clings till the breath departs—happy is he who forsakes that thirst.

sanskrit: cāritram ātmanaḥ paśyaṃś candraśuddham anāmayam dharmātmā labhate kīrtiṃ pretya ceha yathāsukham
english: Seeing his own conduct pure as the moon and free of blemish, the righteous-souled man wins renown, and both here and hereafter abides in happiness.

sanskrit: rājñas tad vacanaṃ śrutvā prītimān abhavad dvijaḥ pūjayitvā ca tad vākyaṃ māṇḍavyo mokṣam āśritaḥ
english: Having heard the king's words, the brahman grew glad; and honoring that speech, Māṇḍavya betook himself to liberation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃśīlaḥ kiṃsamācāraḥ kiṃvidyaḥ kiṃparāyaṇaḥ prāpnoti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yat paraṃ prakṛter dhruvam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what character, of what conduct, of what learning, devoted to what end, does a man attain the abode of Brahman, that which is beyond Nature and abiding?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca mokṣadharmeṣu nirato laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yat paraṃ prakṛter dhruvam
english: Bhīṣma said: Devoted to the duties of liberation, eating sparingly, his senses subdued, he attains the supreme abode, that which is beyond Nature and abiding.

sanskrit: svagṛhād abhiniḥsṛtya lābhālābhe samo muniḥ samupoḍheṣu kāmeṣu nirapekṣaḥ parivrajet
english: Having gone forth from his own home, the sage, even-minded toward gain and loss, indifferent though objects of desire press close upon him, should wander as a mendicant.

sanskrit: na cakṣuṣā na manasā na vācā dūṣayed api na pratyakṣaṃ parokṣaṃ vā dūṣaṇaṃ vyāharet kva cit
english: Neither by eye, nor by mind, nor by speech should he do any harm; neither openly nor in secret should he ever utter a word of reproach.

sanskrit: na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāni maitrāyaṇagatiś caret nedaṃ jīvitam āsādya vairaṃ kurvīta kena cit
english: Let him do no harm to any living being, and walk the way of friendliness; having come into this life, let him bear enmity toward none.

sanskrit: ativādāṃs titikṣeta nābhimanyet kathaṃ cana krodhyamānaḥ priyaṃ brūyād ākruṣṭaḥ kuśalaṃ vadet
english: Let him endure harsh words and never grow indignant in any way; though raged against, let him speak kindly, and though reviled, let him answer with good wishes.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ prasavyaṃ ca grāmamadhye na cācaret bhaikṣacaryām anāpanno na gacchet pūrvaketitaḥ
english: Neither rightward nor leftward let him make rounds in the midst of the village; not engaged in the round of begging, let him not go to a place arranged for beforehand.

sanskrit: avakīrṇaḥ suguptaś ca na vācā hy apriyaṃ vadet mṛduḥ syād apratikrūro visrabdhaḥ syād aroṣaṇaḥ
english: Modest in bearing and well-guarded, let him not utter with his speech anything unkind; gentle let him be and not harsh in return, trusting and free of wrath.

sanskrit: vidhūme nyastamusale vyaṅgāre bhuktavaj jane atīte pātrasaṃcāre bhikṣāṃ lipseta vai muniḥ
english: When the smoke has died, the pestle is laid aside, the embers are spent, the household has eaten, and the passing-round of dishes is over, then let the sage seek his alms.
